subject: Spanska 4
title: Environment and sustainability
sourceSummary: Vocabulary and reasoning around environmental issues and sustainability, a common discussion theme in upper-secondary modern languages.

questions.opener: A central concept in every environmental debate.
questions.explanation: "El calentamiento global" means "global warming" — a fundamental concept in environmental vocabulary.

questions.opener: A concept often contrasted with "los combustibles fósiles" (fossil fuels).
questions.explanation: "Las energías renovables" means "renewable energy sources" (e.g. solar and wind power), the opposite of "los combustibles fósiles" (fossil fuels).

questions.prompt: Which word best fits the sentence: "Debemos reducir nuestra huella de ___ para proteger el planeta."
questions.opener: A common expression for how much of a resource a person consumes: "huella de...".
questions.explanation: "La huella de carbono" (the carbon footprint) is a central concept in sustainability discussions and refers to the amount of greenhouse gases caused by a person or activity.

questions.prompt:
Read the sentence: "Aunque muchos jóvenes se declaran preocupados por el cambio climático, pocos están dispuestos a cambiar sus hábitos de consumo."

What is the point of the sentence?
questions.opener: The word "aunque" (although) marks a contrast between two things.
choices: There is a gap between young people's concern about the climate and their actual behavior
Young people don't care at all about climate change
All young people have already changed their consumption habits
Climate change only affects older generations
questions.explanation: "Aunque" (although) marks the contrast between being worried and actually changing one's behavior — the sentence's point is precisely this gap between attitude and action.

questions.opener: A concept that combines economic, social and environmental considerations.
questions.explanation: "El desarrollo sostenible" means "sustainable development" — a concept that balances economic, social and environmental needs.

questions.prompt: Which word means "shortage" (e.g. of water), as in "la escasez de agua"?
questions.opener: A word that often appears in the context of drought and resource shortages.
questions.explanation: "Escasez" means "shortage", as in "la escasez de agua" (water shortage). The opposite, "abundancia", means "abundance".

questions.prompt: Correct the errors in the sentence: "Si nosotros no hacemos nada ahora, las futuras generaciones sufrirán las consecuencia de nuestro inacción."
questions.opener: Two grammatical errors are hiding here: one noun in the wrong number, and one word with the wrong gender/article.
questions.answer: Si nosotros no hacemos nada ahora, las futuras generaciones sufrirán las consecuencias de nuestra inacción.
steps: "Las consecuencia" has the wrong number — the plural definite article ("las") requires a plural noun: "las consecuencias".
"Nuestro inacción" has the wrong gender — "inacción" is a feminine noun (la inacción), so the possessive must be "nuestra", not "nuestro".
The rest of the sentence is correctly built as a real si-clause (type 1): si + present indicative (hacemos), main clause in the future (sufrirán).
Full sentence: "Si nosotros no hacemos nada ahora, las futuras generaciones sufrirán las consecuencias de nuestra inacción."

questions.prompt: What environment and sustainability vocabulary should you know at this level?
questions.opener: Key concepts for discussing environmental issues at a more advanced level.
questions.answer: el calentamiento global = global warming · el cambio climático = climate change · las energías renovables = renewable energy sources · los combustibles fósiles = fossil fuels · la huella de carbono = the carbon footprint · el desarrollo sostenible = sustainable development · la escasez (de agua) = the shortage (of water) · contaminar = to pollute · reciclar/el reciclaje = to recycle/recycling · reducir el consumo = to reduce consumption · concienciar = to raise awareness. A useful phrase for discussion: "Aunque muchos... pocos están dispuestos a..." (Although many... few are willing to...) for expressing a gap between attitude and action.

questions.opener: A problem often linked to the Amazon rainforest.
questions.explanation: "La deforestación" means "deforestation", the process of clearing forest.
"La biodiversidad" means "biodiversity", the variety of species in an ecosystem.

questions.opener: An important part of a sustainable lifestyle.
questions.explanation: "El consumo responsable" means "responsible consumption", consciously choosing what and how much to consume.

questions.prompt:
Read the sentence: "Muchas ciudades han empezado a prohibir los vehículos más contaminantes en sus centros urbanos."

What does the sentence mean?
choices: Many cities have started banning the most polluting vehicles from their city centers
Many cities have built more roads for cars
Many cities have stopped running public transport
Many cities have banned bicycles from the city center
questions.explanation: "Muchas ciudades han empezado a prohibir los vehículos más contaminantes en sus centros urbanos" means "many cities have started banning the most polluting vehicles from their city centers".

questions.opener: The place where trash that isn't recycled ends up.
A fundamental concept in environmental and sustainability discussions.
questions.explanation: "Los recursos naturales" means "natural resources" — e.g. water, forests, and minerals.

questions.prompt: What does the verb "agotar" mean, as in "agotar los recursos"?
questions.opener: A verb describing what happens when a resource runs out.
questions.explanation: "Agotar" means "to deplete/exhaust completely": "agotar los recursos" means "to deplete the resources".
